steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Buongiorno, dear residents.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: After several months of preparation, Carnevale will be held as scheduled on the evening of November 9th, where hundreds of thousands of citizens will be on the streets celebrating the one-year anniversary of Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: According to the Carnevale organizing committee, all the beast floats have been assembled at the port, and will be moved to the expansion plate today in preparation for the night parade.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The street theater competition has also concluded. The most popular team will gain the privilege of illuminating the floats on the behalf of every citizen here on Carnevale night...

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Other shortlisted plays will also be performed on both sides of the parade path alongside the floats.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The committee hopes that everyone will cooperate and maintain the floats' mystery before their forms are unveiled on Carnevale night! Please rein in your curiosity, and do not sneak a look, photograph or spread any float-related information!

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: In other news: On November 5th, a traffic accident occurred on Quinta Strada in the port district late at night with one injury reported. The vehicle responsible escaped after crashing.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The police quickly got the scene under control, and restored order in the area. The incident did not have any serious consequences, so there is no need for our dear citizens to worry.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Presently, the police have established a special task force to investigate and identify the vehicle responsible, and the case should be closed within the next few days. Citizens who discover any relevant clues should contact the police as soon as possible...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Texas.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You're back.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Just a brief visit, I'll go back to court later.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: How's Leon?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: The doctor came here three times... only for routine check-ups though—at least his condition isn't getting worse, I suppose?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'm guessing you had trouble dealing with that case yesterday?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The case was closed... in a way I didn't want, with a way I was powerless to stop.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Texas, I don't recall you having a habit of tuning into the afternoon news.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: The situation isn't as optimistic as the news make it out to be, right?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: We found some clues and locked onto some suspects, but we haven't made any other progress.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Who called the police that night?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The info we got was all fake. Hard to investigate.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Maybe I could help? I know quite a few people in the city, those from the famiglia...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Grazie, Texas... I know you've been keeping an eye on the whole thing.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Your mere presence in Volsinii was enough to strike a nerve in every influence in the city. Some were angry, while others got a wake-up call, and we managed to turn things around.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But a year has passed, and we're in Nuova Volsinii now. In a new city without the famiglie, the 'Last Texas' can't really do much.

spans.text: But a year has passed, and we're in
Volsinii now. In a new city without the famiglie, the 'Last Texas' can't really do much.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: In other words, the 'Last Texas' shouldn't be allowed to do much here.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Nurse
steps.text: Signorina Texas, there's a phone call at reception for you.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Who is this?
Haha. Need a ride, Texas?
I won't wait too long.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: The sun was so strong the last two days. What's with the sudden heavy downpour?
You wouldn't be carrying an umbrella if you were really surprised.
Here, over here.
On the hood of a cab, and under a huge black umbrella, the driver casually plays with the car keys in her hand.
Haha, you got here quickly.
Da quanto tempo, Texas.
The driver slowly lifts her umbrella, revealing a sharp crescent—an unrestrained smile. She then nonchalantly tosses the umbrella aside and salutes a greeting to Texas.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Lappland.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: The weather got me thinking about our old home. The nights and rain in Volsinii.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Yeah. The weather here has always been great until today.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But you seem to have seen this rain coming, Texas.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I just prepare for the worst. We're still in Siracusa after all. Having just one rainy day after so many days of fine weather is pretty rare.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: What exactly happened with that accident?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You mean the one with the Bellone wolf pup? Hahahaha. Surely you're not suspecting that I did it with my car right here?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I wouldn't be surprised if it was you.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You wouldn't be here right now if you had nothing to do with it.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: ...I do know a few things.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Willing to have a ride with me?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Hmph. Why not? I wouldn't be standing here otherwise.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You know, I thought you'd be nice and shade me from the rain with your umbrella.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You seem like you're enjoying the rain. Didn't want to spoil your fun.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hahaha, that's the Texas I know.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Are you going to just stay on your car like that? In such a big rain with no spectators? Not tired?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh? Haven't you been watching me the whole time?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Get in the car, Texas. Our destination is quite far away, so it'll be quite a long drive.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Right, I prepared a gift for you in the passenger seat.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I saw the snacks... I don't have the appetite right now.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It's alright, it's not millefoglie this time.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I've long changed my tastes.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Though I know you're still obsessed with those old habits of yours.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Texas? Back so soon?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: It's me.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Demetri?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You shouldn't have clearance to come in here.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: There's always a way. You can't prevent me from seeing Leon forever.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I brought some flowers. Hmm, is there a vase in here that might fit?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We used to have roses like this at the Bellone residence, remember?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Don't look at me like that, Lavinia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: The police have thoroughly investigated my travel itinerary on your orders for the past two days, every single detail.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But they found no clues linking me to that accident.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'm not so stupid to think you'd commit a crime yourself.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: My city hall colleagues told me how they recently received an entity ownership change application from Saluzzo Vino... Why are you collaborating with Alberto, Demetri?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Since this city—or I should say, you—have been so unwelcome, I had to figure out my own way to stay here.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Doesn't it comply with the city rules?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Perfectly.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Then, wouldn't it be better if I stayed within your sights?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You've already deployed enough officers here to watch every step I take, any contact I make, every order I give.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I should be allowed a visit.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I was the one nursing Leon back to health whenever he was sick.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: The Bellones won't give up trying to enter the city, Lavinia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But in any case, there is no need or reason for me to hurt Leon.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'll accept your flowers in his place.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But I'm sorry. As an officer of the law, I will not allow a potential suspect to meet the victim in private.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leon's safety is closely tied to the city's.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: No one can say where the chaos will come from next.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: —This is what you wanted me to see?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I see the rain earlier wasn't heavy enough.
Fire.
The speeding cab suddenly brakes when it nears the fire, leaving clear skid marks on the still-wet ground.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Would you believe me if I said I brought you here to extinguish the fire?
The monstrous wolf breathes flames and thick smoke into the air.
The giant beast-shaped float burns, the bright fire light standing out against the dull dark sky.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Lappland... how much do you know about this?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Suspecting me?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: No. You would have chosen a more classical and conspicuous method.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You'd be standing in the fire right now at least, not next to me.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Haha, you know me so well.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Too bad the workers and police are pretty quick to act. I think the fire'll be put out quite soon.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: They should be thanking that burst of heavy rain earlier, otherwise the fire might have already burned down Nuova Volsinii Port to cinders.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: No matter how big the fire is, it doesn't change the fact that it's here in the city.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Leontuzzo and the others wanted to give the new city a brand new festival to help build a collective identity.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: A car accident that left the Mayor in critical condition and a giant blaze breaking out at the logistics port just before Carnevale. That's enough to keep the civilians up awake at night.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Doesn't it feel like some kind of omen, a proclamation, or even a provocation?!

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: How much do you actually know, Lappland? What's your objective?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Tsk, tsk. You sound anxious—Why?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Wasn't Nuova Volsinii the proving grounds Signora Sicilia promised to the youths?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: An experiment is bound to produce mixed results.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: As the first witness on the scene, I can tell you for certain the Bellone pup's car crash was purely an accident.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You've been watching over him at the hospital, and his condition has already stabilized, right?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: So what's causing your anxiety?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I look forward to your answer, Texas... at Carnevale.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: No matter what you're planning...

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'll be keeping an eye on you for Lavinia.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hahaha, then sit tight.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I have no interest in wasting my time with those officers.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: H-How can that be?!

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: The parade float... got lit up on fire along with the goods—

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: Ugh—?!

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Calm down, it's me. The police are on their way here, so stay out of their sight.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: L-Lyudmila?

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: Where did you go the night before yesterday? No, wait. Why are you here?

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: I have more questions than you, Sommer.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Where did you go after the accident?

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: I-I went to find Eirene. She knocked me out cold and then locked me inside the warehouse—Well, a lot happened, and it was a hell of an escape.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: *sigh* Come with me. Everyone's attention is focused on the float now. My smoke will cover our tracks, and no one'll spot us.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: Why's there a burn spot on your jacket?

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: The fire... was y-your...

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: My doing.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: The police would have discovered the truck and its contents if I hadn't done it there and then. It was the only way.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Enough, we'll talk when we're safe. Those officers—

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: W-Wait, Lyudmila. Someone just went by over there... Eirene?!

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: Who's the guy next to her?!

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Eirene Lavazza, and Alberto Saluzzo. Could you both please kindly explain what brings you here just two hundred meters away from the fire?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I don't see a need to explain myself.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: If you want my answer, have the judge bring the evidence and arrest warrant to me first.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I'll be waiting.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: We'll get to it, Signor Saluzzo.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: It's true we don't have any evidence to pin you as the culprit, but this doesn't mean you're completely unrelated to the case.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: As for you, Signorina Eirene Lavazza.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: The float burned nearly to nothing, but we managed to collect some fragments.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: We'll send them for analysis later, but we're basically certain that the vehicle used for the float was a truck from your group.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: As the head of the Truckers' Union, you'll have to come with us for our investigation.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: ...Signor Saluzzo.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Signorina Lavazza, our previous agreement still stands.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I believe you have no link to the matter, but do be careful about what you say once you leave this place.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Otherwise, even I won't be able to help you.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Don't you find this place familiar, Texas?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But this time, the one standing in the defendant's dock is neither you or me...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: What a shame.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Even if we take the judge's word that this case is suspected of endangering the city's public safety, there's no reason to let all of these people in here.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: A trial for a truck driver, and the audience gallery seats are filled with made men from two famiglie with conflicting interests.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hahaha. I'm liking Nuova Volsinii more and more, Texas.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But I have to say, this trial was put together more quickly than I thought.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Probably a special procedure. Carnevale is tomorrow, so it's understandable they'd want to settle the case ASAP.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Do you know this Eirene woman?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You don't have to probe me, Texas.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I only met this poor little driver once, but I can guess how she ended up here.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You mean, she's innocent?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I didn't say that.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Isn't this scene a regular occurrence in the swamp of Siracusa?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It swallows everyone up eventually. Not everyone can escape it like you did...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Either you get killed and silenced, or you hide within the mud and drag out a meaningless existence.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Texas, do you believe that Nuova Volsinii offers a third way of life?

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Silence.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: In accordance with the New Urban Management Act, the Nuova Volsinii criminal court will commence with the Nuova Volsinii Port Arson Public Prosecution Case, number 00278. Court is in session.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Defendant, please state your identity for the record.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Eirene Lavazza. Born in Sicilia, currently a member of the Truckers' Union and living in the Trucker Camp on Viale Alito, Zona Torino.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: What did they mean our testimony would be invalid in court?

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Does that mean we can only sit here and wait for the results of her trial?

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: I wanted to go even more than you do, Lyudmila. After all, it's because of me that Eirene...

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: But you heard about what happened at the police station, right? She didn't say anything... so we can't just barge in there ourselves.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: She believes in the government and the courts, and thinks she can prove her innocence...

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Do you believe that'll happen?

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: I believe in her.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Wait for me here, Sommer. I'll call the other guys to go with us. We should be standing by her side right now no matter what.
Sommer slumps over on the ground cradling his head, watching Lyudmila leave.

If he hadn't helped the Venezias transport their goods without telling Eirene, if that car accident hadn't happened, if he hadn't asked Eirene for help, if he had managed to break free from his chains earlier and make it to the port in time...
He's the reason why this incident happened, but now the one standing in court awaiting trial is his best friend, and his... daughter.
He gropes around in a pocket for a business card. He doesn't know who stuck it in the gaps of his campervan door.
The card only has an address on it—'Terza Zona Porto'.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: Eirene, I know you outsmart me in most cases...

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: But this time, I know I can help you out for sure...
He stands up and leaves the campground alone.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Eirene Lavazza. Identity matches registered information.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: The blaze at Zona Porto yesterday caused serious property damage, put the lives of dozens of workers at the port at risk, and gravely threatened the public safety of Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Carnevale is right around the corner, and this incident will immeasurably affect public opinion.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: The court has examined the evidence submitted by the police, and found that the great wolf parade float, the source of the fire, has obvious traces of arson.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: The vehicle was from the Truckers' Union. The police reviewed the trucks' shift schedules and found out it was not deployed at that time, and should not have been in Porto Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: You, head of the Truckers' Union, also just happened to be at the scene of the crime—

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Signorina Lavazza, you are our prime suspect. You have every right to defend yourself.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Your Honor, I'm happy to tell you everything I know.
Eirene calmly explains how yesterday's fire had no links to any one from the Truckers' Union.
But the judge's expression becomes even gloomier.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: The judge can't help her, even if he wants to.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Of course. As long as the real culprit doesn't show up, her attempt to defend herself will be for naught.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: *sigh* Woe, the poor lady! Don't you want to help her out, Texas?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You could stand up and vouch for her, etcetera. The court might be lenient on her if it's you.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I know what you're thinking, Lappland.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Nuova Volsinii's laws absolutely cannot be trampled upon or scorned like that. They strove to make these rules a reality.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Then I fear you can only sit back and watch everything unfold, or...
Lappland sends Texas a provocative look, eager to try something.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I could care less for your boring rules. Want me to help you out?

spans.text: could care less for your boring rules. Want me to help you out?

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: *ahem* Please hold on. The court has just received a supplementary list of new witnesses who would like to provide testimony.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Uh... A-Alberto Saluzzo?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: What's wrong, Your Honor? As a legal citizen who has completed his identity registration in total compliance with the New Urban Management Act, surely my testimony will be valid in court?

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: O-Of course. Please proceed to state your testimony for the record.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Signor Saluzzo, are you intending to provide evidence to the court to prove that Eirene was indeed related to the fire?
Alberto does not answer. His gaze falls on the opposite site of the witness box. Venezia Junior and the other Venezias are sitting on the left side of the audience.
Alberto's eyes turn to the seat behind Venezia Junior—there sits his own daughter, the banished Saluzzo.
She crosses her legs, grins, and waves to him as if no one else is in the room.
Next to her is Texas.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: (Ciao.)

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Texas, my dear father is watching us. Stop being so reserved and wave along.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Signore? Signor Saluzzo? Please continue with your testimony.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I was there as well, and I can attest that Signorina Lavazza did not start the fire.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: Terza Zona... should be here...
Sommer?

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: The boss made us wait here for you.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Come. He wants to see you.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: Are you from the Venezias? Or the Saluzzos? Or the Medicis...?

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Tch.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: This'll help Eirene, right?

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Right up ahead.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: The container in that corner. Just open the door and go in.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: Alright.

a.text: Eirene. I'm sorry for not telling you, but I already made arrangements for Guri.
You know how I kept asking for more shifts and saved quite a bit of cash. It should at least be enough to pay for two years of Oripathy treatment and her school fees.
The school isn't too far from our camp, so it'll be easier to look after her this way too.

I did take you in at the start, but compared with all the help you've given us all these years it's hard to say who has helped the other more. Eirene, it's not fair they've got a spotlight on you now.
It's time you think about yourself too, haha.
I wanna say I've never been much of an idealist. After all, I've seen enough in this life, I know very well what I can do or can't...
I'm just a tiny supermarket owner and driver who hopes we can all live a peaceful life... this is also why I was willing to follow you here.

The shop's no more, but we can always move to a new place and figure out a new way of life. There's no need to waste our time on those guys who ruined our lives. Everyone gets their share of bad luck, so there's no need to blame anyone.
We just have to stay far away from the troubles.
Fortunately, you helped us all find a good spot.
I bet Guri will like it here.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I guarantee you my testimony is absolutely true. As I said earlier, she was with me the whole time from yesterday before noon until the fire happened at the port.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Two Saluzzo Vino vineyards will soon welcome our first harvest. I hope the Truckers' Union will allocate a fleet to help transport our fresh grapes.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: This is why we were at the port to check things out. My employees can vouch for us as well.

steps.name: Gallery Mafiosi
steps.text: (Sounds of agreement)

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: In other words, Signorina Lavazza has a strong alibi.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: (Claps) Magnifico.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: My astute padre has tied the Truckers' Union to the Saluzzos.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: That poor driver will have to do his bidding in future.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I don't think it'll end just like that.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: The truck came from your union. We checked the shipping schedule and it wasn't slated with any arrangements for the last two days. So why did it show up at the port and become one of the floats?

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Signorina Lavazza, even if you truly did not start the fire, as the head of your union it is your responsibility to explain the illegal usage of this car.
I can testify for Signorina Lavazza on that point.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Signor Venezia?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Your Honor, please take a look at the customs declaration form in the supplementary evidence you received earlier. The truck was transporting tires for Venezia Trucking.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: This is it. Go in.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: He's waiting.
The shipping container door lies ajar, and all Sommer can see is a faint light flickering inside the dark interior.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: So, who on Terra is helping me... and Eirene?

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Enough questions, vecchio.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: Go in and you'll find out at once.

steps.name: Mafioso
steps.text: You want to help that driver, and so do we. That's all you need to know.
Sommer puts his hand on the door, and hesitates.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: Can you guarantee—
There is no one available to answer him. The mafiosi already left, leaving him on his own.

a.text: Eirene, I don't have brains or guts like yours.
Which is why I was so surprised but also worried when you promised Judge Lavinia and Mayor Leontuzzo you'd be the head of the union.
It meant we were going to get into tons of trouble... and sure enough we did.
But back then you told me what we were starting wasn't actually a 'union' to help city hall handle the famiglie, but an 'association' to provide mutual aid to anyone in a similar situation as us.
You always say I was the one who took you in, but we all know it was you who gave me another chance at life.
I'm not saying we're even now, I owe you so much.
Eirene, if a day comes where I can help you out, I won't hesitate at all.
I don't want Guri to think her papa as an ungrateful person.
I tried to be a good role model for her.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: Signor Venezia, I'm sure you're clear what your statement means, right?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Signor Saluzzo claims he submitted testimony out of his responsibility as a citizen, but this incident actually involves Venezia Trucking.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The demand for our vehicles here has spiked in the last two months because of Carnevale, and we had to order an impromptu shipment of automotive consumables from the other cities.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: This newly-arrived batch of goods has already cleared custom, and the Truckers' Union was helping us do a last-mile delivery. It was an impromptu request, which is why they haven't updated this job to their schedule.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Signorina Lavazza, do correct me if I got anything wrong.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: You're right, we do have the paper trail, if needed.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: As for why that truck was found at the port amongst the parade floats, we don't know who did it yet, so I implore the police to continue their investigation.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Though at least, the Truckers' Union did not use their truck illegally, and Signorina Lavazza was merely a bit negligent in this whole affair.

steps.name: Judge
steps.text: We'll verify the information.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh, the poor driver's pretty lucky. We're so close to the end of the tunnel.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: The pivotal testimonies from my father and Venezia Junior are enough to clear Eirene of suspicion. Nothing will happen to her.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: But the suspect has now become an outsider.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Eirene's the actual person involved, but she can't even get a word in. The courtroom's turned into an exclusive stage for the Venezias and Saluzzos.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: These two factions are clearly fighting under the table, but they seem to have a tacit understanding once they're in court.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Everyone knows that's how the mafia works.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: They want to claim complete innocence, and seize the Truckers' Union for themselves at the same time.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Of course. After all, we haven't found the actual person who started the fire.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Unless... they'll never find the person ever again.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hahaha, the famiglie never consider what the persons involved are willing to offer when they want something in return.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: ...I have to contact Lavinia.
He takes in two deep breaths, pushes the shipping container door open, and goes in.

steps.name: Sommer
steps.text: ...Nobody's here?
Inside is a sole lamp and chair with no one else.
Sommer is stunned.
He decides to wait. As long as he can help Eirene this way...
He's willing to wait.

a.text: Eirene, I like this new city.
I hope Guri likes it too. At the very least, I've prepared a better environment for her here.
Grazie, Eirene.
Look, I better get going. I've never gotten a late delivery on my record.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Terza Zona... He should be here...

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Blyat! How am I supposed to find him in such a huge place?
Lyudmila anxiously pops in and out of alleys created by the containers, trying to locate any trace of Sommer.
Until she hears voices nearby.

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: So? Where are you going on vacation after Carnevale?

steps.name: Mafioso B
steps.text: Volsinii? The old-school musical theaters are all there. I'm planning to go to the more sophisticated establishments.

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: I rather go to Terni. I hear the clubs there have male Perro striptease dancers from Bolívar.

steps.name: Mafioso B
steps.text: Tsk. You better tuck your tail in if you do, Saluzzo.

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: Hah. Want me to recommend you some ticket vendors in Volsinii?

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: You're a pretty good guy, and get work done quick. If you can't get along with the Venezias, come find me and I'll introduce you to some guys.

steps.name: Mafioso B
steps.text: I'll pass. Want a smoke?

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: Heh, this lighter's pretty easy to use.
Lyudmila sees the two yapping openly, but she could not care any less what they are talking about.
Her sole target is the golden lighter one of them is playing with in his hand.
She recognizes that lighter, and knows the two are not its owners. It belongs to a driver who doesn't smoke.
What Lyudmila doesn't know is that it originally belonged to a famiglia associate.
After a roller-coaster ride, it ends up back in the hands of the mob once more.
